@graph.name: How to Evaluate and Hire the Best Custom Website Developer
@graph.description: Evidence-based checklist for evaluating custom website developers before hiring, focusing on verifiable quality signals rather than self-reported claims.

step.name: Test Lighthouse scores on their portfolio sites
step.text: Open Chrome DevTools → Lighthouse → Mobile on 2–3 websites from their portfolio. A developer claiming '90+ Lighthouse scores' should have verifiable evidence. Anything below 70 on mobile is a red flag for a custom website specialist.

step.name: Check accessibility with axe DevTools
step.text: Install the free axe DevTools Chrome extension and run it on their portfolio sites. A quality custom website developer should have zero critical or serious WCAG violations on core pages.

step.name: Review their GitHub code quality
step.text: Ask for a GitHub repository from a recent project. Look for: TypeScript usage, component organisation, no hardcoded API keys, proper error handling, and meaningful commit messages. Code quality reveals engineering depth that portfolio screenshots cannot.

step.name: Ask a technical SEO question
step.text: Ask: 'How do you implement JSON-LD structured data on a Next.js blog?' A developer who can answer this in detail (with specific schema types and placement strategy) has real technical SEO knowledge. Vague answers suggest SEO is an afterthought.

step.name: Request their project brief template
step.text: A professional custom website developer has a documented project brief process. Ask to see the template they use to scope projects before signing a contract. Lack of a process document signals a disorganised engagement.

mainEntity.name: What makes a website developer 'the best'?

acceptedAnswer.text: Verifiable evidence: Lighthouse 90+ on mobile (testable), WCAG AA compliance (axe DevTools verifiable), GitHub portfolio with TypeScript/Next.js code, JSON-LD structured data on every page type, and a documented project process. Claims without evidence are worthless.

mainEntity.name: How much does a custom website cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Custom website pricing: 5-page business website: $3,499–$5,999. E-commerce: $6,999–$12,999. Complex platform: from $12,999. Hourly: $29/hr (direct, no agency markup). 40–60% below comparable agency rates while maintaining identical technical standards.

mainEntity.name: Does Core Web Vitals affect Google search ranking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Google confirmed Core Web Vitals (LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms) as ranking signals in the Page Experience update. Custom Next.js websites consistently score 90+ Lighthouse on mobile; template sites typically score 40–70 due to unoptimised themes and third-party scripts.
